about: A command a phone or the website sends a runner and waits on (an archive, a star, a reply button, a card's answer, Stop), from the tap to the runner saying how it went: idle, sending (the mutation hasn't answered), queued (the backend has it, the runner hasn't taken it), taken, done (with the thread it made, if any), failed (with why, if it said) or timedOut (nothing heard in 20 s, still listening). input is the events in order, times in ms: tap, sent (the backend's command id), sendFailed (the mutation threw), row (phone:command's answer: pending, taken, done, failed, or null once it's gone from the backend), deadline (the clock), reconnected (the connection dropped and came back), cancelled (the backend took it back) and settle (a moment after done). expect is where it ends and whether the control takes taps (locked). The iPhone (ThreadbearKit PendingCommand.swift), Android (kit PendingCommand.kt) and the website (web/src/command.ts, whose waiting is queued or taken and whose slow is timedOut).

cases.name: a tap starts sending, and takes no more taps
the backend's id makes it queued
a pending row leaves it queued
the runner taking it makes it taken
done, with the thread it made, stays locked until it settles
done settles back to idle
a send the backend refuses fails with why, and can be tapped again
the runner refusing it fails with its note
a refusal that says nothing has no reason, for the control to give its own

differs.web: Says "unknown error" (command.ts); the phones leave it empty so each control says it in its own words ("The runner couldn't archive that thread.").

cases.name: a second tap while sending is ignored, and doesn't restart the clock

differs.web: A send that hasn't reached the backend goes slow and stays locked: the website's Convex client keeps retrying it. A phone's client can be thrown away on coming back from the background (and then never answers), so a phone lets it be tapped again.

cases.name: a second tap while queued is ignored
a second tap while done is ignored until it settles
queued just short of the deadline is still queued
queued with nothing heard in 20 s times out, still listening, and takes taps again

differs.web: Slow stays locked until it's dismissed with its ×; a phone's next tap is its dismiss.

cases.name: the runner taking it restarts the clock
taken with nothing more heard in 20 s times out

differs.web: Slow stays locked until it's dismissed with its ×; a phone's next tap is its dismiss.

cases.name: a timed-out command still lands when the runner answers
a timed-out command the runner then refuses fails
a timed-out command the runner then takes is taken, on a fresh clock
a timed-out command can be tapped again

differs.web: Slow stays locked until it's dismissed with its ×; a phone's next tap is its dismiss.

cases.name: a send that hasn't reached the backend in 20 s times out, and its late id still lands
a send that times out and then throws fails
a row before the backend's id is ignored
a late row after done is ignored
a failed command can be tapped again
a command gone from the backend reads as done

differs.web: phone:command answers null for a pruned command; the website's useCommand never hands that to command.ts, so it has no such event.

cases.name: a reconnect restarts a queued command's clock, as it couldn't hear meanwhile

differs.web: The website's Convex client reconnects by itself under the same subscription, so it has no reconnect event.
